title: Ὄφις πατούμενος καὶ Ζεύς
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 291. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ὄφις ὑπὸ πολλῶν πατούμενος ἀνθρώπων τῷ Διὶ ἐνετύγχανε περὶ τούτου.
sentences.tr: Ophis hypo pollōn patoumenos anthrōpōn tōi Dii enetynchane peri toutou.
sentences.l: A snake, being trampled by many men, kept appealing to Zeus about this.
sentences.n: ἐντυγχάνω with the dative is to fall in with a person and so to approach him with a request — the regular word for petitioning. The present participle πατούμενος keeps the trampling going on and on, and the imperfect ἐνετύγχανε does the same for the petition.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ Ζεὺς πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν· « Ἀλλ’ εἰ τὸν πρότερόν σε πατήσαντα ἔπληξας, οὐκ ἂν ὁ δεύτερος ἐπεχείρησε τοῦτο ποιῆσαι. »
sentences.tr: Ho de Zeus pros auton eipen· « All’ ei ton proteron se patēsanta eplēxas, ouk an ho deuteros epecheirēse touto poiēsai. »
sentences.l: And Zeus said to him: « But if you had struck the one who trampled you first, the second would not have attempted to do this. »
sentences.n: A past contrary-to-fact condition: aorist indicative in the 'if' clause, aorist indicative with ἄν in the conclusion — 'if you had struck…, he would not have attempted'. τὸν πρότερόν σε πατήσαντα is an articular participle, 'the one who trampled you first'; the second accent on πρότερόν comes from the enclitic σε leaning back on it.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι οἱ τοῖς πρώτοις ἐπιβαίνουσιν ἀνθιστάμενοι τοῖς ἄλλοις φοβεροὶ γίνονται.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti hoi tois prōtois epibainousin anthistamenoi tois allois phoberoi ginontai.
sentences.l: The story shows that those who stand against the first to tread on them become formidable to the rest.
sentences.n: The house formula ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι, 'the story shows that…'. ἀνθίσταμαι takes the dative of the party stood against, and that party is here an articular participle, τοῖς πρώτοις ἐπιβαίνουσιν — the men who tread first, with the trodden-on left unexpressed. φοβεροί is active in sense, 'causing fear', not 'afraid'.
